title: Capability Exposure Accounting for Threshold-Based Encrypted Backup Recovery: research artifact
description: Release 4.1.20 of the research artifact and manuscript for "Capability Exposure Accounting for Threshold-Based Encrypted Backup Recovery" (Samarjeet Malik, Shaurya Pratap Singh), the version the authors are submitting for publication to the International Journal of Information Security. The only change from version 4.1.19 is in the declarations: the "Use of large language models" statement now also discloses that OpenAI's ChatGPT was used to provide critical manuscript feedback, identify potential inconsistencies and suggest editorial revisions, which the authors independently evaluated. No theorem statement, proof, result, figure or reference changed. The artifact code (artifact/) is byte-identical to version 4.1.1 (10.5281/zenodo.24060229), which reproduces every result; the clean re-run of the archived v4.1.1 tag is in reproduction_logs_v4119/. A pinned container (Dockerfile) is built and run by a GitHub Actions workflow. The composition theorem (Theorem 24) is restricted-adaptive (guessing factor L), not fully adaptive, and an independent review of it is outstanding. No physical erasure, refinement proof or production readiness is claimed. Source: https://github.com/SamarjeetMalik/threshold-backup-capability-accounting (tag v4.1.20). Previous version: 10.5281/zenodo.24112284 (v4.1.19).
notes: Code and artifact (artifact/) under MIT; the manuscript, figures and plot data under CC BY 4.0. Springer class and style files keep their upstream terms.
